note: Four classes of connectivity after the collapse of the old Internet. A network's class decides what a scene may attempt before CWN Hacking is even relevant: a closed network needs a body, a badge or a medium in the room.

perimeter.name: the Plato/EISS perimeter
perimeter.subsystem_codename_note: AEGIS was floated as the firewall subsystem designation; it is NOT canon until the author confirms it.
perimeter.operated_by: Europol, on behalf of the EU institutions that own, fund and audit it

networks.name: the old Internet
networks.description: Fragmented, semi-abandoned digital wilderness: autonomous agents, rogue processes, compromised infrastructure, dead services that still answer. Connecting is a risk, not a resource.

networks.name: closed organisational networks
networks.description: Agencies, corporations, laboratories and hospitals run isolated private networks, often air-gapped. A terminal, a badge, an implant or a removable medium has to be in the room before any intrusion is attempted.

networks.name: EuroNET
networks.description: The EU-maintained public network behind the perimeter: email, forums, blogs, OSINT. Deliberately constrained, slow and conservative — a security trade-off, not backwardness. No unconstrained autonomous agents.

networks.name: data couriers
networks.owner: whoever holds the media or the person
networks.description: Physical transport of storage media and of data held in people. Interception, handoff and authenticity are investigation beats, not hack attempts.
